tools.description:
Inspect one Port OS event subscription by its exact ID returned by subscription_list.

Returns its safe query, source endpoint, catalog name and lifecycle status. A retained active subscription establishes registration; it does not prove that any client has received or acted on a camera event.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "control" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Control connected devices and services, retrieve results, and capture camera snapshots. Choose exactly one target: id for a specific endpoint/group, or query us…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "control" is 8425 chars, far longer than this server's median (1407). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: control, endpoint_manage, endpoint_query, group_manage, group_query, subscription_list · Private data: control, endpoint_manage, endpoint_query · Public sink: control, endpoint_manage, endpoint_query, endpoint_show, group_manage, group_query · Destructive: control, endpoint_manage, group_manage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: control, endpoint_manage, endpoint_query, group_manage, group_query, subscription_list · Private data: control, endpoint_manage, endpoint_query · Public sink: control, endpoint_manage, endpoint_query, endpoint_show, group_manage, group_query · Destructive: control, endpoint_manage, group_manage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
